incident_management_quick_reference.overview: Quick reference guide for SDLC incident management using Bob with ServiceNow, Ansible, and Terraform integration.

steps.step: ☐ Gather complete incident details from user
☐ Explain fix to user (for user_overload: BOTH scaling + load balancer required)
☐ Execute remediation (playbook OR Terraform scaling + load balancer)
☐ For user_overload: Verify load balancer distributes traffic across instances

type.name: Performance
type.symptoms: Slow response times, timeouts, degraded performance

type.name: User Overload
type.symptoms: Backend overloaded, high CPU/memory, too many users/connections
type.remediation_approach: Terraform horizontal scaling + Nginx load balancer (BOTH required)

critical_steps.step: 1. Scale backend to multiple instances using Terraform
2. Add Nginx load balancer to distribute traffic
3. Verify traffic distribution across all instances

type.warning: Scaling alone is insufficient - load balancer is REQUIRED for traffic distribution

type.name: Deployment
type.symptoms: Deployment failures, broken functionality after deploy

type.name: Backup/Restore
type.symptoms: Need for backup or data restore

urgency_levels.level: High - Critical issue, immediate attention required
Medium - Significant issue, needs timely resolution
Low - Minor issue, can wait for scheduled maintenance

impact_levels.level: High - Affects multiple users or critical systems
Medium - Affects single user or non-critical system

issue.name: ServiceNow MCP fails
issue.check: Verify .env has SERVICENOW_* variables
Test ServiceNow connectivity

issue.name: Ansible playbook fails
issue.check: Verify playbook and inventory are ABSOLUTE paths (relative paths always fail)
Do NOT set the cwd parameter — causes 'spawn /bin/sh ENOENT'
For shell module: avoid Go template syntax (e.g., docker --format "{{.Names}}") — use docker ps --format json or docker inspect instead
Verify connectivity to target hosts
issue.fallback: Use manual commands or alternative playbook

issue.name: Playbook not available
issue.check: List available playbooks in ansible/playbooks/
Check if similar playbook exists
issue.fallback: Use manual commands or create new playbook

issue.name: Root cause unclear
issue.check: Run health check for more details
Check application logs
Review recent changes

issue.name: Terraform state lock (stale lock from timed-out apply)
issue.check: Identify lock ID from the error message: 'Error acquiring the state lock'
Confirm the prior apply actually completed by running terraform_show — if state is consistent, the lock is stale
issue.resolution: Use Ansible run_adhoc to force-unlock: module='shell', args='cd [absolute-tf-dir] && terraform force-unlock -force [LOCK_ID]'
issue.warning: Only force-unlock if you are certain the prior apply process is no longer running

issue.name: Terraform -replace flag not working via terraform_apply plan_file
issue.check: The plan_file parameter accepts a saved plan file path only — it does NOT accept raw flags like -replace
issue.resolution: Use Ansible run_adhoc as fallback: module='shell', args='cd [absolute-tf-dir] && terraform apply -auto-approve -replace="resource.type.name"'
issue.note: Docker image rebuilds triggered this way may exceed MCP call timeouts — this is expected for large images

issue.name: Terraform apply times out (Docker image build)
issue.check: Docker image builds can take minutes and exceed MCP call timeout
Run terraform_show after timeout to verify whether the apply actually completed
If a stale state lock remains, use force-unlock (see above issue)
issue.note: The infrastructure may be fully deployed despite the timeout — always verify state before retrying

issue.name: Fix doesn't resolve issue
issue.check: Re-run diagnostics to see current state
Verify fix was applied correctly
Consider alternative root causes

template.name: incident_created
template.text:
ServiceNow incident [INC_NUMBER] created successfully. - Priority: [PRIORITY] - Short Description: [DESCRIPTION]
Now I'll begin diagnosis to identify the root cause.

template.name: diagnosis_complete
template.text:
Diagnosis complete. [FINDINGS_SUMMARY]
Root cause: [ROOT_CAUSE]
I'll now [REMEDIATION_ACTION] to resolve this issue.

template.name: seeking_confirmation
template.text:
I recommend [ACTION] because [REASON]. This will [IMPACT].
Shall I proceed?

template.name: verification_complete
template.text:
Verification complete. [RESULTS_SUMMARY]
Before: [BEFORE_METRICS] After: [AFTER_METRICS]
The issue has been successfully resolved.

template.name: incident_closed
template.text:
Incident [INC_NUMBER] has been resolved and closed.
Summary: - Root Cause: [ROOT_CAUSE] - Actions Taken: [ACTIONS] - Verification: [VERIFICATION_RESULTS]
[FOLLOW_UP_ACTIONS if any]

best_practices_summary.practice: Update ServiceNow after each major step
Use appropriate playbooks for incident type
For user overload: ALWAYS include load balancer with scaling - scaling alone is incomplete

success_criteria.criterion: Root cause identified through systematic diagnosis
User informed and satisfied with resolution
